articles.title: Donald Trump suspende sanções previstas contra parceiros comerciais da Rússia | G1
articles.standfirst: O recuo de última hora gerou críticas dentro do partido dele e aumentou a tensão com a Ucrânia.
articles.summary: O recuo de última hora gerou críticas dentro do partido dele e aumentou a tensão com a Ucrânia.
articles.body:
O presidente Donald Trump suspendeu as sanções previstas contra parceiros comerciais da Rússia.

O recuo de última hora gerou críticas dentro do partido dele e aumentou a tensão com a Ucrânia.

Faltavam menos de 48 horas para sanções entrarem em vigor quando o presidente dos Estados Unidos publicou o decreto suspendendo a ordem. No documento, Donald Trump disse que a decisão é do interesse dos Estados Unidos, mas não explicou qual.

As sanções foram aprovadas há um mês pelo Congresso americano, onde o partido de Trump, o republicano, tem maioria. Previam tarifas de até 100% sobre todos os produtos importados pelos Estados Unidos dos 5 países que mais compram gás ou petróleo bruto da Rússia.

China e Índia já tinham manifestado preocupações. A medida também valeria a qualquer país que a partir daquela data comprasse as commodities russas.

A intenção era aumentar a pressão econômica em cima da Rússia para tentar forçar o Kremlin a negociar o fim da guerra contra a Ucrânia, que começou no início de 2022.

A mudança de posição de agora provocou críticas de parlamentares americanos e do presidente da Ucrânia. Volodymyr Zelensky classificou a decisão como uma recompensa para Putin.

O aumento do custo de vida nos Estados Unidos pode estar por trás da suspensão das sanções.

No dia 3 de novembro acontecem as eleições para o Congresso americano e pesquisas apontam que a rejeição ao governo Trump atingiu o maior patamar desde que ele foi eleito. O número é puxado por eleitores descontentes com os preços mais caros.

Desde o início da guerra no Irã, em fevereiro, o valor do diesel subiu 68% nos Estados Unidos. A conta do frete mais caro foi repassada aos consumidores.

Em setembro, a inflação americana chegou a 3,7% em comparação com setembro de 2025.

Na semana passada, Trump anunciou um acordo com Vladimir Putin para liberar diesel da Rússia no mercado internacional.

No Farol da Barra, o candidato do PL recebeu o título de cidadão soteropolitano, concedido pela Câmara de Vereadores de Salvador.

Depois, o candidato discursou e disse que, se eleito, vai focar no combate à violência.

"Porque no meu governo, vagabundo vai ficar preso. Ladrão de celular vai começar com oito anos de cadeia e vai ter que trabalhar para pagar sua estadia no presídio. Eu vou jogar pesado com a marginalidade. Eu vou declarar PCC, Comando Vermelho e milícias como organizações narcoterroristas".

articles.title: Manifestantes fazem ato de apoio à eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: A mobilização foi divulgada como "Bloquinho do 22" e aconteceu na Avenida Marechal de Castelo Branco
articles.summary: A mobilização foi divulgada como "Bloquinho do 22" e teve início por volta das 19h. O ato ocorreu na Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco, na Zona Norte de Teresina, uma das principais
articles.body:
Manifestantes se reuniram neste sábado (17), em Teresina , para participar de um ato de apoio à candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) à Presidência da República. O candidato disputa o segundo turno das eleições de 2026 contra Lula (PT), marcado para o dia 25 de outubro.

A mobilização foi divulgada como "Bloquinho do 22" e teve início por volta das 19h. O ato ocorreu na Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco, na Zona Norte de Teresina, uma das principais vias da capital piauiense.

A concentração dos participantes aconteceu nas proximidades de um shopping e ocupou as duas faixas da avenida. Imagens registraram uma grande presença de apoiadores ao longo do percurso. Os participantes usavam predominantemente roupas nas cores verde e amarela e carregavam bandeiras do Brasil.

Manifestantes fazem ato de apoio à eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro em Teresina — Foto: Gustavo Cavalcante

Durante o ato, o trânsito ficou interrompido na Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco. Os motoristas precisaram utilizar rotas alternativas para seguir viagem enquanto a manifestação acontecia.

Por volta das 20h, o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL) informou nas redes sociais que deixava a Bahia com destino ao Piauí para acompanhar o ato. Nikolas foi reeleito deputado federal por Minas Gerais e, pela segunda vez consecutiva, foi o mais votado do país, com 3,1 milhões de votos.

No primeiro turno das eleições, realizado em 4 de outubro, Flávio Bolsonaro recebeu 47,03% dos votos válidos no Brasil, enquanto Lula teve 45,16%.

No Piauí, Lula recebeu 70,99% dos votos válidos. O percentual foi o maior registrado entre os estados brasileiros. Em nove municípios piauienses, o petista obteve mais de 85% dos votos válidos.

Já Flávio Bolsonaro teve 24,09% dos votos válidos no Piauí. Os dados são do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

articles.title: Confeiteira morre com câncer raro em Goiás | G1
articles.standfirst: Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares, de 45 anos, foi diagnosticada com câncer em julho de 2025 e compartilhava nas redes sociais sua luta contra a doença e a fé na recuperação.
articles.summary: Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares, de 45 anos, foi diagnosticada com câncer em julho de 2025 e compartilhava nas redes sociais sua luta contra a doença e a fé.
articles.body:
Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Veri Pires

Veridiana Pires de Oliveira Soares, de 45 anos, morreu durante o tratamento de um câncer raro, em Caldas Novas , na região sul de Goiás. Dona da Veri Pires Confeitaria Artesanal, ela havia suspendido as encomendas para se dedicar à recuperação. A confeiteira lutava contra a doença desde julho de 2025, quando recebeu o diagnóstico.

Veri, como era conhecida, morreu neste sábado (17). Ela foi diagnosticada com carcinoma adenoescamoso de colo uterino metastático , uma forma agressiva de câncer cervical. Nas redes sociais, a confeiteira costumava compartilhar informações sobre a doença, o tratamento e a recuperação, além de demonstrar a fé na cura em momentos de oração com a família.

"Pausa para a cura. Lutando contra um tipo raro de câncer. Compartilho meu processo com fé, coragem e propósito", diz a biografia do perfil dela no Instagram.

A morte de Veri causou comoção nas redes sociais entre familiares e amigos. Ela foi lembrada como uma mulher guerreira.

"Mãezinha, que Deus te recebe com o maior amor do mundo. Você foi a pessoa mais forte que conheci e passou por tudo com um sorriso no rosto. Descanse em paz, minha mãe. Eu te amo para sempre", escreveu o filho, Iago Calixto.

Natural de Caldas Novas, Veri viveu por um período em Gramado, no Rio Grande do Sul, antes de retornar à cidade natal.

O velório foi realizado neste sábado (17), na Paz Universal, em Caldas Novas. O sepultamento ocorreu no Cemitério Parque São Jorge.

articles.title: Indians to benefit as Canada moves to award points for job offers in high wage occupations; those with Canadian experience will benefit more
articles.summary: Canada has reintroduced Express Entry points for qualifying job offers in high-wage occupations and will also award additional points for eligible
articles.body: Canada has reintroduced Express Entry points for qualifying job offers in high-wage occupations and will also award additional points for eligible Canadian work experience in these occupations.From Nov 3, 2026, eligible candidates can receive up to 70 additional points (under the comprehensive ranking system – CRS) for Canadian work experience in high-wage occupations on top of their standard experience score, this could give them up to 150 points in this category.However, it should be noted that candidates can receive points for either eligible Canadian work experience with extra points for experience in designated high-wage occupations; or a job offer in one of these occupations. Canada’s immigration agency will award whichever score is higher - candidates cannot combine the two.Further, a longstanding procedural hurdle will also be removed. From Nov 3, a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) will no longer be required for a qualifying job offer to receive the new Express Entry points or to meet job-offer requirements under the Federal Skilled Worker Program and Federal Skilled Trades Program.However, the change does not mean that every job offer will be accepted automatically. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), in an announcement made on Friday night, states that it will continue assessing whether offers are genuine and meet programme requirements, with measures to guard against fraud.Express Entry mechanism is the system under which aspirants who apply for permanent residency, are placed in a pool, and are ranked based on the Comprehensive Ranking Score (CRS). Those meeting the cut-off score in that particular draw are given an invitation to apply for permanent residency. Indians constitute a significant chunk of those who are invited to apply for permanent residence (PR) under the Express Entry route.Announcing the changes late at night on Friday, Canada’s Immigration Minister Lena Diab said: “Canada is competing globally for people with the skills we need to build a prosperous economy and stronger public services. These changes will help us identify, attract and retain the skilled newcomers who are best positioned to succeed in Canada, while making the Express Entry system more targeted and responsive to our labour market needs.”The high-wage classification is based on the occupation's National Occupational Classification (NOC) wage benchmark, rather than simply an individual's actual salary. For Express Entry, an occupation qualifies as high-wage when its median wage is at least 1.3 times the median wage of the overall Canadian workforce. The applicable wage tier determines the additional points available.For Indian professionals, the announcement could have significant implications. Those already working in Canada in software development, information technology, engineering, nursing, finance and other eligible high-wage occupations may be able to improve their CRS rankings through qualifying Canadian work experience. “A software engineer with three years of Canadian experience, for instance, could gain 40 additional points under the new high-wage experience rules, according to Kubeir Kamal, a regulated Canadian immigration consultant.The picture could be less favourable for Indian applicants who are still outside Canada, lack qualifying Canadian work experience or are employed in occupations that do not meet the new wage criteria. International graduates on post-graduation work permits who work in lower-wage or entry-level positions could also find it harder to compete as candidates eligible for the new points move ahead in the pool. The impact will depend on each applicant's occupation, experience, existing score and the requirements of future invitation rounds.Candidates already in the Express Entry pool will have their scores automatically recalculated to account for eligible Canadian work experience. The recalculation could take up to two weeks, during which invitation rounds will be paused. However, candidates claiming job-offer points must update their Express Entry profiles with the required information before Nov 3.The changes build on Canada's wider effort to align economic immigration with labour-market priorities. In Dec 2025, the country announced measures for medical doctors, including a dedicated Express Entry category for doctors with Canadian work experience. In Feb 2026, it announced new and renewed category-based selection priorities for sectors including healthcare, skilled trades, research, transportation and education.Top three source countries for Canadian Permanent ResidencyCountry2025CountryJan-June (2026)India98,830India44,335Philippines25,230Philippines13,475Cameroon22,925China9,630The Times of India reached out to Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants (RCICs) to understand how the changes could affect Indian applicants, who stands to gain or lose, and what candidates should do before the new rules take effect.Kubeir Kamal: 'This is the biggest change to how Express Entry ranks candidates since job offer points were removed in 2025'Kubeir Kamal said the announcement would benefit some skilled workers already employed in Canada but could intensify competition for international graduates and people working in occupations that do not qualify for the new high-wage points.“This is the biggest change to how Express Entry ranks candidates since job offer points were removed in 2025. For Indians already working in Canada in software, engineering, nursing or finance, it is good news. A software engineer with three years of Canadian experience gains 40 points from November 3. The people who lose ground are international graduates and workers in jobs that are not on IRCC’s high-wage list, such as cooks, truck drivers, retail supervisors and even construction electricians. Their scores stay the same while others move ahead, so they should expect higher cut-offs.“My real concern is fraud. Job offer points were removed last year to curb fraud. Now they are back, worth up to 100 points, and the LMIA is gone. Under the previous LMIA process employers had to undergo checks that could include advertising the position to demonstrate recruitment efforts, wage assessments and an evaluation of the potential impact on the Canadian labour market. IRCC is replacing all of that with short checklist, applied by officers already buried in backlogs. I hope IRCC has strong measures in place to validate and verify these offers. Candidates abroad, including many in India, are the easiest targets for anyone selling fake offers. My advice is simple. A genuine Canadian employer will never ask you to pay for a job offer. If someone does, walk away and report it.”Kamal's warning underscores an important distinction: removing the LMIA requirement does not mean that job offers will automatically be accepted or that employers and candidates will no longer face scrutiny.IRCC has said it will continue assessing whether job offers are genuine and meet programme requirements, with measures intended to protect the integrity of the immigration system.Ken Nickel-Lane: 'A rather smart shift in policy on many levels'Ken Nickel-Lane views the changes as a strategic move that could benefit high earners, expand Canada's tax base and make the country more attractive to senior personnel working for multinational companies.“We will see an Express Entry program change adding points for high wage earners under a new Labour Market Integration factor to a maximum of 150 points for individuals earning at least 1.3 times above the average median wage of the Canadian work force, taking effect Nov 3. For those that qualify and currently do not have the points to get an invitation to apply for permanent residence with the current trends this is great news. From a government strategy perspective, it’s also quite interesting. It’s a relatively simple change from an implementation perspective, and for those that focus on immigration as a means to increase our tax base and increase consumer spending it is also very sensible. Higher wage earners pay more taxes and spend more. Arguably, those in higher paid positions, at least in the corporate world are economic drivers unto themselves, the ‘business builders. Not just the best and brightest, but the ‘movers and shakers’.”He also sees potential implications for corporate mobility and Canada's appeal to experienced professionals considering an international move.“This change is a quiet incentive to move more senior personnel into Canadian divisions of those multinational corporations with Canadian entities or looking to establish them. There is now a clearer pathway to Permanent Residence and ultimately Canadian citizenship for senior personnel, increasing the long-term attractiveness of a move, particularly for those looking for an escape hatch from the US under the current administration. Canada now becoming a much more favourable base of operations with easier, and improving access to EU markets under Prime Minister Carney. What initially looked a bit like a blunt instrument change, is upon closer inspection a rather smart shift in policy on many levels.”Nickel-Lane's analysis suggests that the implications may extend beyond individual immigration applications. By creating a more direct route for qualifying high-wage professionals, the changes could influence how multinational employers deploy senior employees across their Canadian and international operations.Rattandeep Singh: 'Is your work in demand and well paid?'Rattandeep Singh described the announcement as one of the most significant CRS changes in recent years, arguing that it changes the emphasis of Canada's economic immigration selection system. IRCC is moving from ‘do you have a job offer?’ to ‘is your work in demand and well paid?’” The high-wage classification is based on the occupation's NOC code and the applicable wage benchmark, rather than simply the salary an individual happens to earn. A candidate cannot necessarily qualify for a higher points tier just by negotiating a higher salary if the occupation itself falls into a lower wage category under IRCC's published criteria, he pointed out.He added that removing the LMIA cuts off much of the market for selling LMIAs to boost CRS scores. Genuine employers, including new ones, can now support candidates without the LMIA process. However, fraud may change shape, from fake LMIAs to fake ‘high-wage’ job offers.Like others, Singh echoed that post-graduate work permit holders in lower-wage occupations may struggle to compete, even with solid Canadian experience. French proficiency draws or additional points for French proficiency will continue to be the saviour for 95% serious applicants.Gurpreet Oshan: Welcome news for skilled professionals, but not everyone benefits equallyGurpreet Oshan said the changes, such as return of points for qualifying job offers, could significantly alter the permanent residence prospects of skilled workers already employed in Canada, including Indian nationals, but warned that the benefits would not be evenly distributed. Candidates without Canadian work experience (such as those applying from India) or those without qualifying job offers may find themselves facing tougher competition against those who have already gained Canadian work experience.”Oshan highlighted the distinction between the wage level assigned to an occupation and the actual salary earned by an individual worker. “One important distinction is that points are based on the occupation’s national median wage, not the individual’s actual salary. This recognizes that newcomers often accept lower-paying positions despite having strong qualifications and professional experience. Their current earnings do not necessarily reflect their skills or long-term economic potential.”She also questioned whether a wage-based approach would always identify the occupations in which Canada most urgently needs workers. “However, this approach also raises an important question. Does a higher-paying occupation necessarily mean Canada is facing a shortage of workers in that field? Not always. Some occupations experiencing genuine labour shortages may not meet the designated wage thresholds. As a result, individuals working in these occupations could find themselves at a disadvantage despite contributing to Canada’s economy and labour market.”Oshan added that removing the LMIA requirement should not be mistaken for removing scrutiny of job offers. IRCC will continue assessing whether employers are genuinely operating businesses, whether they have the capacity to fulfil the offers, and whether the positions are legitimate. “This is particularly important because job offers can now carry substantial weight in determining who receives an invitation. Applicants and employers should expect employment arrangements and supporting documentation to be examined carefully,” she said.“My advice is simple: do not confuse additional points with guaranteed permanent residence. Job offers must still be genuine, and eligibility must be established through credible evidence. “Applicants should carefully review how the changes affect their profiles before making major employment or immigration decisions. A higher CRS score may improve their chances of receiving an invitation, but the responsibility to demonstrate eligibility remains unchanged,” she summed upTalha Mohani: 'Canada has moved from a volume-driven system to a precision-driven system'Talha Mohani stated that Canada is refocusing Express Entry away from paper approvals and onto real economic value by giving extra points to high-wage occupations while completely removing the LMIA requirement for job offer points and program eligibility under FSWP and FSTP. Canada has moved from a volume-driven system to a precision-driven system.“A major benefit of this policy update is that it effectively shuts down the LMIA grey market that has plagued our immigration system for years. By eliminating LMIAs for Express Entry points, the government is wiping out the shadow economy of paid or fraudulent job offers. Points will now be tied strictly to verified salary thresholds against national median benchmarks, taking away the unfair advantage dishonest actors used to have. It is important to note that points are determined by the NOC median wage benchmark, NOT the candidate's personal contract salary. Negotiating a higher salary with an employer will not move a candidate into a higher point tier if the NOC itself falls under a lower median wage classification.”Mohani explained the point-based mechanism in detail. Under the new labour market integration factor, candidates with Canadian work experience in an eligible high-wage occupation can get up to 70 extra CRS points on top of their standard experience score, giving them up to 150 points in this category. Roles paying twice the national median wage get the full 70 extra points, while those paying 1.5 times and 1.3 times get 40 and 20 extra points. For Indian professionals already working in Canada in high-demand fields like IT, healthcare, and engineering, this gives a massive score boost to help them clear high cutoffs and secure an invitation to apply.“It is important to clarify a key technical point: applicants cannot combine or stack points for both a qualifying job offer and high-wage Canadian work experience. IRCC evaluates both under the same labour market integration factor and will automatically give whichever option gives the higher score, capped at 150 points for single candidates or 140 points for those with a spouse. You cannot double-dip on both, but having either option elevated gives high-wage earners a solid route to permanent residence,” he stated.For the large population of Indian temporary workers in Canada, the takeaway is clear: Express Entry is no longer about just holding a job offer on paper, but about proven earning power, specialized skills, and real economic contribution (including building competitive profiles through language proficiency or provincial pathways).What candidates need to know before November 3The changes will affect candidates differently depending on their occupation, Canadian work experience, qualifying job offers and existing CRS scores. Based on the insights given by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants, the following points need to be kept in mind.Additional points will be tied to designated high-wage occupations. Under the new Labour Market Integration factor, eligible Canadian work experience in a qualifying high-wage occupation can attract additional points. Qualifying job offers in designated high-wage occupations can also earn points.Job-offer points will return, but the LMIA will no longer be required for the specified purposes. From November 3, a qualifying job offer will no longer need an LMIA to receive the new Express Entry points or to meet job-offer requirements under the Federal Skilled Worker Program and Federal Skilled Trades Program. The job offer must still be genuine and meet applicable programme requirements.The occupation's wage benchmark matters. Eligibility for the new high-wage points is based on IRCC's published occupation list and the median wage benchmark associated with the occupation, rather than simply the individual's actual salary. The government defines a high-wage occupation as one with a median wage of at least 1.3 times the median wage of the overall Canadian workforce.The two routes cannot be stacked. Candidates cannot combine the points for a qualifying job offer with the additional points for high-wage Canadian work experience under the same Labour Market Integration factor. The system will award whichever option gives the higher score, subject to the applicable maximum.Existing candidates should check their profiles. IRCC will automatically recalculate scores for candidates already in the Express Entry pool. However, candidates seeking points for a qualifying job offer must update their profiles with the required information before Nov 3, 2026. Invitation rounds are expected to pause for up to two weeks while the system recalculates scores.Lower-wage workers and some international graduates may face tougher competition. Candidates whose occupations do not qualify for the additional points may find that their relative ranking falls as other candidates move ahead. Canadian work experience, education, language proficiency and other CRS factors will remain relevant, but the effect of the reforms will depend on each applicant's circumstances.Fraud risks and verification remain important. The removal of the LMIA requirement does not mean that job offers will be accepted without scrutiny. IRCC will continue checking whether employers and positions are genuine and whether offers meet programme requirements. Candidates should be wary of anyone demanding payment in exchange for a job offer.The latest changes also come as Canada seeks to manage immigration levels while responding to economic requirements and pressure on housing and public services. The policy change does not guarantee permanent residence to any candidate. Applicants will still need to meet the relevant programme requirements and receive an invitation to apply.For Indian applicants, the central question will be whether their occupation and experience qualify under the revised rules. Professionals already working in Canada in designated high-wage occupations may benefit from a stronger CRS score, while candidates in lower-wage jobs or without Canadian work experience could face a more competitive selection environment.

articles.title: Kolkata stampede: Sharp spell turns Chorbagan puja pandal into death trap
articles.summary: Hour-long Kolkata downpour linked to retreating monsoon caused Chorbagan puja pandal stampede; Met office says dry weather through Oct 21.
articles.body: KOLKATA: A sudden and unexpectedly sharp spell of shower, that turned into a torrential downpour and lasted nearly an hour on Saturday evening, spelt disaster for revellers at the Chorbagan puja pandal. It started with a drizzle but soon turned heavy, forcing visitors to rush inside the pandal for shelter. But as the crowd in and around the pandal grew, most waiting for the rain to lose intensity, the shower turned heavy.Even though sporadic rain had been predicted by the Met office till Saturday, it was expected to be restricted to drizzles. “It was triggered by the retreating wedge or retreating monsoon that causes sporadic rain. Even though monsoon has started retreating and it is expected to be completely dry from Sunday, Kolkata received two sharp spells on Saturday. While the one during the afternoon was relatively light, the evening spell turned out to be consistent and lasted for a significant period of time,” said H R Biswas, deputy director general of meteorology.Also read: 19 killed in Kolkata stampede; CM Suvendu announces jobs, Rs 25 lakh for kinThe rain turned the ground soggy making foothold difficult which contributed to the stampede, said a weather official. “The rain was not heavy but retained intensity for more than 45 minutes,” said the official. Had it lessened quickly, the disaster may not have happened, he added.It also turned out to be a dampener on a day when lakhs had been out on the streets. While puja revellers were left worried about further such spells, the Met office said the dry weather from Sunday will continue at leas till Oct 21, which is Dashami.“Chances of moderate or heavy rain are virtually nil over the next four days. They will not recur,” said Biswas.In meteorology, a retreating wedge refers to the weakening and clearing phase of a cold air damming (CAD) event. A “wedge” is a shallow, dense layer of cold air trapped against a mountain range (most famously the eastern side of the Appalachian Mountains in the US).When this air mass “retreats”, it means the weather system that caused the trap is moving away, allowing the cold, stubborn layer to erode and normal regional temperatures to return.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: An Oklahoma landowner turned his family's cattle farm into a 130-acre haven for pollinators after noticing fewer monarch butterflies
articles.summary: For nearly 70 years, Patrick Bell's family farmed land in Johnston County, Oklahoma, primarily raising cattle.
articles.body: For nearly 70 years, Patrick Bell's family farmed land in Johnston County, Oklahoma, primarily raising cattle. Over time, the fields became dominated by introduced grasses and other vegetation, while Bell began noticing fewer monarch butterflies during their autumn migration. He also observed a decline in other butterflies and pollinators. Rather than accept the changes, he decided to restore part of his family's property as wildlife habitat. With help from conservation agencies and local organisations, Bell spent seven years experimenting with planting methods and land-management techniques. The effort resulted in 130 acres being managed for pollinator conservation, with native grasses and flowering plants providing habitat for butterflies, bees and other pollinators.How an Oklahoma landowner turned his family's cattle farm into a pollinator havenBell's family had operated the farm for generations, raising cattle on land that had gradually become dominated by introduced vegetation. These included Bermuda grass, fescue, rye, vetch and Johnson grass.Bell remembered seeing hundreds or even thousands of monarch butterflies passing through southern Oklahoma during their autumn migration when he was growing up. About 15 years ago, he began noticing that fewer butterflies were appearing. In the later years of the family's farming operation, he also observed fewer other butterfly species and pollinators.In 2016, Bell attended a lecture organised by the Oklahoma Native Plant Society, where monarch conservation expert Orley "Chip" Taylor spoke about declining butterfly and pollinator populations. The event helped inspire the formation of the Oklahoma Monarch and Pollinator Collaborative, of which Bell became a co-founder.Bell had already established a small pollinator garden at his home in Edmond, Oklahoma, but wanted to expand his efforts. He decided to use his family's land to create a larger area of habitat for pollinators.How Bell began restoring 130 acres for native plants and pollinatorsBell sought assistance from the US Fish and Wildlife Service's Partners for Fish and Wildlife programme, the Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) and the Oklahoma Prescribed Burn Association.He divided the land into sections and began experimenting with methods to remove unwanted vegetation and establish native plants. His initial approach involved applying herbicides, conducting prescribed burns and tilling the soil before planting native seeds.However, the results were mixed. Some native grasses and flowering plants failed to establish as successfully as he had hoped, prompting him to consult conservation specialists and research alternative methods.With advice from the NRCS and the US Fish and Wildlife Service, Bell determined that using a no-till drill, which places seeds into the soil without conventional tilling, would be important to improving the results.Funding provided by the Chickasaw Nation enabled the nearby Pontotoc County Conservation District to supply him with an agricultural no-till drill. The equipment helped Bell refine his planting strategy and expand the approach across the restoration area.How the family cattle farm became a pollinator habitatThe restoration took seven years of experimentation, research and changes to land management. According to the US Fish and Wildlife Service's report published on July 29, 2026, Bell has treated and replanted 118 acres, while the remaining 12 acres already had native vegetation. Together, the 130 acres are managed for pollinator conservation.The restored land contains native grasses, flowering plants and wildflowers that provide habitat for pollinators. Photographs accompanying the federal agency's account show a bumblebee on an Engelmann's thistle growing on the property, along with fields of native yellow wildflowers and areas where the new planting approach was used.Bell also plans to continue using prescribed fire to manage the habitat, working with the Johnston County Prescribed Burn Association.Bell wants the restored land to help future conservationistsBell hopes the property will serve an educational purpose alongside its role as pollinator habitat. He wants the land to remain available in perpetuity for students and future land managers to learn about habitat restoration and conservation practices.The project involved cooperation between Bell and several organisations, including federal and state conservation agencies, local conservation districts and the Chickasaw Nation. Their support helped him access technical advice, equipment and resources while he worked through the challenges of establishing native vegetation across the property.Bell has described the effort as a labour of love and credited the people and organisations that helped him make progress. After seven years of work, the restored acreage provides an area managed specifically for native vegetation and pollinator habitat.“I hope that my story can inspire others,” Bell said, according to the US Fish and Wildlife Service.You use AI every day. articles.title: San Diego is weighing a $4.2 billion redevelopment of 48.5 city-owned acres with 4,254 homes, a $526.4 million arena and $460.3 million in infrastructure and park improvements
articles.summary: San Diego is advancing a proposed $4.2 billion redevelopment of 48.5 acres of city-owned land around the Pechanga Arena, with plans for thousands of
articles.body: San Diego is advancing a proposed $4.2 billion redevelopment of 48.5 acres of city-owned land around the Pechanga Arena, with plans for thousands of homes, a new entertainment venue and major public infrastructure improvements. According to the City of San Diego’s official Midway Rising project page, the proposal includes 4,254 housing units, a 16,000-seat arena and new parks and public spaces in the Midway District. On October 16, 2026, the City Council’s Land Use and Housing Committee unanimously voted to advance the proposal, bringing the long-delayed project closer to consideration by the full City Council.What the $4.2 billion redevelopment includesThe Midway Rising proposal aims to transform the existing Sports Arena property into a mixed-use neighbourhood combining residential buildings, entertainment, retail, parks and improved streets. The development team is expected to finance the estimated $4.2 billion project, which would replace the ageing arena and parking-dominated site with a more integrated urban district. The housing component includes 2,000 affordable homes and 2,254 market-rate units. The affordable housing allocation includes at least 200 permanent supportive housing units intended to serve people who need additional support to maintain stable housing.The plan also proposes up to 130,000 square feet of retail and commercial space, creating room for shops, dining and other businesses. The wider development is designed to make the area more walkable, improve connections to public transport and provide more public spaces for residents and visitors. The project is being developed by Midway Rising, a consortium that includes Zephyr, The Kroenke Group, Legends and Chelsea Investment Corporation.A new arena and hundreds of millions for infrastructureA central feature of the proposal is a new multipurpose arena costing an estimated $526.4 million. Designed to accommodate 16,000 people, the venue would replace the existing Pechanga Arena as the area's main entertainment destination. The development also includes $460.3 million in infrastructure and public improvements. These are expected to cover street upgrades, pedestrian-friendly routes, parking facilities, parks and other improvements in and around the site. The plan provides approximately 14.5 acres of combined park and public space, offering recreational areas alongside the new housing and commercial development.Construction would take place in phases. The first phase is expected to deliver the new arena alongside affordable and market-rate housing. The existing arena would continue operating until its replacement is ready to open, allowing scheduled events to continue during the transition. The overall development is expected to take years, with the city’s Independent Budget Analyst estimating that full buildout could take about 20 years, although the developer has projected a shorter construction period of around 10 to 15 years.Why the city is prioritising housing and public amenitiesThe proposal reflects a financial trade-off for San Diego. Instead of prioritising immediate rental income from its land, the city is seeking substantial private investment in affordable housing, entertainment facilities and infrastructure. Under the proposed arrangement, the developer would make investments upfront, while the city would receive revenue through arena ticket fees and rent from market-rate housing and retail as different phases are completed. The timing and amount of those payments would depend on construction progress and the project's financial performance.The city has also proposed an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District to help fund infrastructure costs. Under this arrangement, increases in property tax revenue above an established baseline could be used to reimburse eligible development infrastructure expenses over time. The city’s Independent Budget Analyst estimates that the developer could be reimbursed for up to $378 million of its infrastructure spending through the proposed financing district. The arrangement means the public benefits would be delivered before the city receives the full financial returns. The proposed agreement therefore includes provisions for oversight as the project progresses.What happens nextThe project has faced years of delays and legal challenges, including disputes concerning coastal building-height restrictions. In September 2026, California Governor Gavin Newsom signed legislation intended to help clear the way for the redevelopment while retaining environmental review requirements. The October 16 committee vote marks another important step, but it does not constitute final approval by the full City Council. The proposed development agreements and related financing arrangements must still move through the remaining approval process before construction can begin.If approved, Midway Rising would reshape a major city-owned property into a residential and entertainment district, with thousands of homes and significant public improvements. Its eventual impact will depend on whether the developer delivers the promised housing, infrastructure and public spaces while managing the financial and construction challenges of a multibillion-dollar project.You use AI every day. articles.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats, French mayor; Netanyahu says no ‘compelling evidence’
articles.summary: Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats, Palestinian olive harvesters and a visiting French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, with
articles.body: Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats, Palestinian olive harvesters and a visiting French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, with vehicles belonging to diplomats from France, Belgium and Poland targeted in the Taybeh area.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later claimed there was a lack of “compelling evidence” surrounding the attack on European diplomats, appearing to suggest that the incident was part of a “coordinated smear campaign”.Footage showed one diplomatic vehicle being pelted with stones, with a window smashed. According to testimonies, seven masked settlers surrounded the vehicle and demanded identification documents before attacking it.The incident came a day after masked settlers allegedly assaulted American photojournalist Heidi Levine while she was covering the olive harvest.Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said Belgium's consul general to the Palestinians, French and Polish diplomats, and a French mayor were among those targeted. A Belgian vehicle was also damaged during the incident."As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice. Impunity for violent settlers must end," Prevot said in a statement posted on X.Bernard Baudoux, the 78-year-old mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, said masked settlers attacked him while he was joining Palestinian farmers in harvesting olives as a gesture of solidarity with the local community."I was thrown to the ground," Baudoux told Reuters.Speaking to AFP, he said the attackers kicked him and struck him with iron bars while making derogatory remarks about France. He also questioned the Israeli government's response to settler violence."I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government," Baudoux told AFP."The whole world needs to know what's happening," he said. "For me, I'll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here."Israel condemns attack, urges military coordinationIsraeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the incident and described those involved as Israeli rioters. However, he said the visiting diplomats should have coordinated their presence with the Israeli military."Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors’ security," he said in a statement on X.Israeli police said they had opened an investigation into the incident. There was no immediate announcement of any arrests.Netanyahu's remarks came amid mounting criticism of settler violence, with his office urging caution before drawing conclusions about the attacks. His response drew criticism from his main rival in the October 27 elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who accused the government of allowing settler violence to undermine Israel's international standing.The attacks also drew condemnation from Palestinian Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh, who described the incident as an example of the "daily terrorism" faced by Palestinians.Olive harvest becomes flashpoint for violenceThe latest violence comes amid a surge in settler attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, particularly during the annual olive harvest, an important source of livelihood and a cultural symbol for Palestinian communities.Bashar Fawadleh, a priest in Taybeh, told AFP that settlers had attacked the harvest and seized olives before assaulting the French mayor. He said one person was struck on the head and required stitches, while an elderly woman in her 70s was also beaten.The incident followed Friday's assault on Heidi Levine, a US photojournalist working for The Washington Post, who was hospitalised after being attacked by masked settlers while covering Palestinian olive harvesters. Reports said she suffered broken vertebrae.Prevot said the repeated attacks on Palestinians, journalists and diplomats required a stronger response."Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said.Belgium, which has announced a ban on imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the Golan Heights, will push for European Union sanctions "against those responsible for this violence and those who support them," Prevot added.Polish Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maciej Wewior said a convoy carrying diplomats, including Polish officials, had been attacked, but the Polish diplomats were unharmed."Attacks on members of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable," he said.Israeli President Isaac Herzog separately contacted Levine in hospital and described the assault as "outrageous and shocking". Israel Gantz, head of an umbrella organisation representing settlers, blamed the recent incidents on "groups of provocateurs and terrorists", saying such actions were damaging the settlers' cause.Settler violence has drawn growing international criticism as Israel continues to expand settlements in the West Bank, territory it captured in 1967. Around 500,000 Israelis live there alongside approximately three million Palestinians. Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are considered illegal under international law.Prosecutions of settlers accused of violent crimes against Palestinians remain rare, despite repeated condemnations by Israeli officials and calls from international governments for those responsible to be held accountable.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump blocking Russia curbs historic moment: Putin envoy
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive a new package of sanctions on Russia is a “historic moment”, a Russian presidential envoy said Saturday.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive a new package of sanctions on Russia is a “historic moment”, a Russian presidential envoy said Saturday. Trump signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, two days before they were due to take effect.The move came amid a clash with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky that has fuelled speculation the US leader is increasingly siding with Moscow nearly five years into Russia’s offensive against Ukraine, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions. “The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, said on social media.The Kremlin and Putin –– who appeared in military uniform Friday and said Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine –– have not yet reacted to the move, which is a major diplomatic win for Russia. The Lindsey Graham Act –– named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill –– targeted Russia’s energy and defence sectors as well as Putin and other senior officials.Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets”. The West imposed massive sanctions on Russia when it launched the Ukraine war in 2022.Russia on Saturday carried out a large-scale overnight attack on Ukrainian infrastructure targets including the country’s largest steelworks in the city of Kryvyi Rih, and vessels using the Ukrainian port of Odesa. The plant is owned by steel giant ArcelorMittal, which suspended operations there in Sept after a series of Russian ballistic missile strikes. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment.In a statement, Russia’s defence ministry said the plant supplied steel products to the Ukrainian military-industrial complex.It said Russian forces had also hit an electricity substation in the northwestern city of Zhytomyr and another steel plant in Zaporizhzhia, a city near the front line.A cargo vessel in the Black Sea was also hit, the ministry said, alleging that it was delivering military cargo to Odesa. Later in the day, the ministry said Russian strikes during the afternoon had hit a vehicle-repair plant in Lutsk.BloombergYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Anthropic has presented its own draft bill to US lawmakers with a plan for regulating artificial intelligence safety and security, in a moment of
articles.body: Anthropic has presented its own draft bill to US lawmakers with a plan for regulating artificial intelligence safety and security, in a moment of heightened concern about the potential risks of the rapidly advancing technology.The proposal suggests govt could block the release of an AI model if it’s determined to imminently risk killing or injuring over 50 people or causing more than $1billion in damage, according to Politico, which first reported on the bill. The threat must be a result of the model creating or releasing a biological weapon, the AI going beyond human control, or a cyberattack, Politico reported.“This bill represents the proposals outlined in Anthropic’s Advanced AI Framework, which we have been advocating for with federal and state lawmakers since June,” a company spokesperson said. The bill would mandate that AI makers must test their models and share findings with the public; it also would require AI companies to allow independent evaluators to routinely review models, the spokesperson said.“Our proposal also grants the federal govt the ability to block or deter dangerous deployments of the most powerful models,” the spokesperson said. “These are sensible policies we believe Congress should act on.”BloombergYou use AI every day. articles.title: How a Brooklyn crypto cop took down a global scam network
articles.summary: By the time Alona Katz hurried home from her office in downtown Brooklyn late on Oct 6, the trap was already set.
articles.body: By the time Alona Katz hurried home from her office in downtown Brooklyn late on Oct 6, the trap was already set. After months of planning, the chief of Brooklyn’s crypto fraud unit was about to orchestrate one of the most sweeping international crackdowns a local prosecutor’s office had ever attempted. The operation, which took place across three time zones, was the culmination of a chase Katz had begun almost as soon as she was appointed chief of Brooklyn District Attorney’s Virtual Currency Unit three years ago.At 2am, dozens of servers that Katz’s team had targeted started going down. She would get no sleep that night.As crypto use has become more widespread, the global crypto fraud economy has exploded in size. In 2025, reported US losses from cryptocurrency fraud reached $11.4 billion, roughly triple from three years earlier, according to the FBI.Before the Brooklyn DA opened the VCU office, victims who sought help from the New York Police Dept were often told to go elsewhere because the NYPD didn’t understand the scams, Eric Gonzalez, the Brooklyn District Attorney, said in an interview.Frustrated as the number of fraud victims soared, Gonzalez decided to set up a special unit to handle it, and hired Katz in 2023 from the Manhattan DA’s cybercrime and identity-theft bureau. Katz, in her 40s, doesn’t have a background in computer programming. She reads poetry, and most of her family are artists.“I was the black sheep for going to law school,” she said.Her phone lit up as soon as she started her new job. Katz soon noticed a pattern in the calls coming into her office. Many victims were from Brighton Beach and Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn communities heavily populated by Russian and Ukrainian immigrants. The scammers, who typically conversed in Russian, identified themselves as fellow immigrants who’d found success trading in the US.The cons were simple. Scammers contacted victims on social networks and persuaded them to invest a few hundred dollars in crypto trades. Small withdrawals were allowed but when victims tried to cash out, they were charged costly fees or ghosted.Katz spent most working hours watching Bitcoin and Tether tokens move between digital wallets, learning the contours of vast underground international fraud networks and how to stop them. Crypto’s transparency aids investigators because transactions are recorded on a public ledger, or blockchain, allowing those with suitable software to follow money between wallets. Over months, Katz and her team identified websites the scammers had set up, and moved to shut them down.Patterns they unearthed include similar branding by these sites, which exposed a cyber infrastructure located in Eastern Europe, including Ukraine. But site seizures proved temporary. Seeking a lasting impact, Katz’s team has developed undisclosed methods to identify servers underpinning the scams.BloombergYou use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Historic French town hall burns, shops looted, tear gas fired as 5,50,00 protest in France
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France, Belgium, Italy and Portugal on Saturday to protest against rising living costs, low
articles.body: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France, Belgium, Italy and Portugal on Saturday to protest against rising living costs, low wages and deteriorating public services, with demonstrations turning violent in several cities.In France, an estimated 550,000 people participated in demonstrations over school conditions, rising fuel prices and the cost of living. Dozens of shops were looted in Paris, Marseille, Nice, Nantes, Bordeaux, Limoges, Lille, Toulouse and Strasbourg, according to news agency AFP.Fires continued to burn in Paris late into the evening as groups of protesters were seen in video footage stoking flames in the streets, while riot police used tear gas and baton charges to disperse crowds.Video footage also showed the destruction of a 143-year-old French landmark after rioters allegedly set it ablaze, causing its roof to collapse into the floors below.In Limoges, local officials said two-thirds of the town hall had been destroyed after protesters set fire to its exterior, describing the damage as a "catastrophe for heritage".At least 195 people had been detained, amid mounting criticism of the authorities' response to the demonstrations. Earlier in the week, police action left a 14-year-old boy with a fractured jaw. Another officer was captured on camera using a headlock on a girl in Alençon, northwestern France, a move now prohibited by law.The protests follow student-led rallies last month and have since expanded into a broader movement against deteriorating schools, the rising cost of living and what demonstrators see as government inaction.French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "sowers of chaos" for disrupting peaceful protests and warned on Saturday that "those who have broken, attacked (police) prefectures, as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished."The unrest extended to other European countries, putting pressure on governments across the European Union.In Brussels, police fired tear gas and used water cannon to disperse demonstrators, accusing them of throwing objects at officers and setting fires. Water cannon were also deployed in Liege, east of the capital, although police did not provide an estimate of the turnout.In Lisbon, tens of thousands of people marched against rising living costs, low wages and the growing difficulty of accessing housing in major cities. House prices in Portugal have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have risen sharply.Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said on Friday that the "government will not yield to shouts from the street". Protesters, meanwhile, accused political leaders of being "out of touch" with their concerns.In Italy, police reported that protesters threw stones and clashed with officers during demonstrations in Milan and Bologna, alongside separate peaceful rallies over the cost of living.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sweet deception: What’s really inside your festive mithai box?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The box is gold-ribboned, the barfi is glossy, and the smell of ghee-laced sweetness is exactly what festive season is supposed to smell like.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The box is gold-ribboned, the barfi is glossy, and the smell of ghee-laced sweetness is exactly what festive season is supposed to smell like. But what you are about to serve may owe more to a chemistry lab than a milk can.Real khoya is humble. According to FSSAI's food product standards for dairy, it is made by rapidly drying cow, buffalo, goat or sheep milk, or milk solids. It must contain at least 55% total solids and at least 27% milk fat on a dry-matter basis, and it must be free of added starch and added sugar.FSSAI's Guidance Note on Traditional Milk Products says that done right, it has a mildly cooked, boiled-milk flavour and a soft, granular body. Cow-milk khoya is pale yellow, while buffalo-milk khoya is white with a brown tinge.Fakes, enforcement officials say, are engineered to imitate exactly those qualities.The recipe, as allegedConsider the raid that Uttar Pradesh's Food Safety and Drug Administration carried out ahead of Raksha Bandhan at a khoya unit in Badshahpur village, Rasoolabad, in Kanpur Dehat. UP food safety officials alleged that detergents, refined oil, talcum powder and hydrogen peroxide were in use.The team recovered 175 packets of skimmed milk powder in seven bags and about 15 litres of hydrogen peroxide. It also found saifolite, destroyed around 100 kg of prepared khoya, and collected samples of 50 litres of milk and 50 kg of khoya for testing.Read the list as a set of workarounds. Skimmed milk powder gives a cheap, milk-like base. Refined or soybean oil stands in for expensive milk fat. In a second unit at Bhola Nagar, Jhinjhak, the same department found 10 litres of refined soybean oil, 10 packets of skimmed milk powder and about 32 kg of prepared khoya.Starch, which FSSAI's guidance note lists among khoya adulterants, adds bulk and density. Talcum powder is alleged to alter texture and appearance, and detergents are alleged to change smoothness and look. Hydrogen peroxide is a bleaching agent.UP officials said titanium dioxide and other whitening agents, liquid glucose, neutralisers and surfactants were also being used to make khoya and other dairy products.These remain allegations, and the samples are awaiting lab results. Not every sweet carries every adulterant. But the pattern is clear: bulk, fat, whiteness and texture, each faked separately and cheaply.The cities connectThis is not a village-only story. On September 29, FSSAI directed all states and Union Territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali, flagging milk products, sweets, snacks, edible oil, beverages and ghee.Under that directive, Delhi's food safety teams destroyed more than 4,100 kg of suspected adulterated khoya and paneer over the previous month, and samples of khoya, paneer, chhena and ghee are being drawn from city markets.Next door in Mewat, officials seized and destroyed more than 10,000 kg of adulterated paneer over the previous month, with around 50 raids in identified production hubs. They said the supply chain runs through Jaipur, Mathura, Gurgaon, Faridabad and Delhi, so what is made in one district can land on the mithai counters of another.Kanpur's numbers, as reported by the UP food safety department, show the scale. Across Kanpur Dehat and Kanpur Nagar, 24 teams inspected units and collected 28 samples, destroying material with an estimated face value of Rs 1.50 lakh.At Hatiya Khoya Mandi, 14 samples were taken and about 430 kg of khoya worth Rs 1.07 lakh was destroyed for unhygienic storage. An FIR was registered at Rasoolabad police station under Sections 274 and 275 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and action to suspend or cancel the registrations of three food business operators has begun.In Noida and Ghaziabad, too, food safety teams have stepped up inspections of milk products and sweets this festive season.A dose of perspectiveNot every box is a hazard. FSSAI's pilot survey of milk products in and around Delhi, conducted between October 15 and November 7, 2019, tested 1,041 samples (438 packed, 603 loose) at the National Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad.According to the regulator's guidance note, the samples showed no major chemical or microbiological safety issues, but predominantly quality and hygiene problems, more often in loose products than in packed ones.Health experts caution that harmful starch, urea-mixed milk, caustic soda and non-approved colours can contribute to acute gastritis, diarrhoea, dysentery, dehydration and kidney inflammation.What you can doFSSAI advises consumers to prefer packed products over loose ones, since the probability of adulteration is higher in loose sales. Its guidance note describes a simple starch check: boil a small piece of khoya in water, cool it and add a few drops of iodine solution.A blue colour indicates starch. FSSAI itself treats such home tests as preliminary indicators, not laboratory proof.If something seems off, FSSAI says complaints can go to its Food Safety Connect portal, WhatsApp 9868686868, email compliance@fssai.gov.in, or toll-free 1800112100.Authorities have been directed to log inspections, sampling and outcomes in real time on FoSCoS and FoSCoRIS.As the Press Information Bureau has noted, FSSAI runs special drives before and during festivals, prioritising adulteration-prone products such as ghee, khoya, paneer and sweets.Until those lab reports land, the festive rule is simple: look past the ribbon.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: UK police rule out probe into Palestine Action post by PM adviser’s wife
articles.summary: Met Police determine X post by Sarah Helm, seen to endorse Palestine Action, does ‘not meet the criminal threshold’.
articles.body:
Police in the United Kingdom have determined that a social media post by the wife of Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s national security adviser that appears to endorse Palestine Action , a group proscribed in the country as a “terrorist” organisation, does not merit a criminal investigation.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson on Saturday said that officers looked at Sarah Helm’s post and ruled that it “did not meet the criminal threshold. No further police action will be taken.”

The police had said on Friday that Helm’s post was “being assessed to determine whether any further police investigation may be required”.

Helm, an author and journalist who is married to National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, wrote on X on Thursday: “God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action.”

Helm made the comment after publisher Faber said this week that its Irish author Sally Rooney could not sell her books in the UK, after she announced her plans to use the royalties to support Palestine Action.

“Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work. To sell a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher,” Faber said in a statement on its website.

“As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format,” the British publisher said, adding that it would continue to sell her work in other countries and regions.

The Campaign Against Antisemitism, a British NGO, had responded on X that Helm’s post was “gobsmacking” and “clearly, the police need to investigate and Ms Helm must face the full force of the law”.

After being asked for comment on Friday, a government spokesperson said Helm’s comments did “not represent the government in any capacity”.

Palestine Action has been proscribed as a “terrorist” organisation since a July 2025 vote by UK lawmakers.

Amnesty International says more than ⁠3,500 people have been arrested in the UK for allegedly supporting Palestine Action since it was banned last year, many of them ⁠for holding up placards.

Palestine Action challenged the government’s decision to ban the group, but the Court of Appeal ruled in June that the proscription was lawful.

articles.title: Completion of roof on Guernsey wildlife hospital marked
articles.summary: GSPCA manager Steve Byrne says hopefully the some of rooms will be ready before the end of the year.
articles.body:
The completion of the roof on a charity's wildlife hospital was marked by a topping out ceremony on Thursday.

The Guernsey Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (GSPCA) has been fundraising for new facilities including the purpose-built hospital designed to treat puffins, hedgehogs, seals and birds, among other wildlife.

GSPCA manager Steve Byrne said now the building was watertight and the roof was on he hoped parts of the facility would be open by the end of the year.

He said "we've been working out of temporary facilities for two years" and the rooms that were nearly done included those dedicated to the care of seals.

The grey seal pup season - when winter storms can run the young animals ashore -runs from October to January and Byrne hoped the new facilities would be available before the charity gets any pups to take care of.

He said the topping out was one of the biggest days in the charities 153-year history.

Byrne said the new building would allow them to give animals the "best of care and the best of facilities and get them back to the wild as soon as possible".

He said the cost of the new facilities had been estimated at between £3.7m and £4m.

Byrne said savings had been made because of donations of things they needed and time from people but they had been some surprises along the way including finding asbestos and the "sewage works needed completely rebuilding".

He said: "We've still got other sections to go... we've got kennels to build, we've got facilities for ferrets to make but this is the main part of what is our big build being the wildlife hospital and we're nearly there."

articles.title: Trump and Netanyahu’s once blossoming bromance sours at a pivotal moment for both men
articles.summary: For years, Israelis driving the country’s highways in the final weeks of an election have seen the same image: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu standing beside President Donald Trump, under the slogan, “A different league.”
articles.body: For years, Israelis driving the country’s highways in the final weeks of an election have seen the same image: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu standing beside President Donald Trump, under the slogan, “A different league.” Less than two weeks before the October 27 vote, the billboards of Netanyahu are back. This time, Trump is not on them. The president still appears in some videos for Netanyahu’s Likud party, but his absence may signal something beyond advertising. Trump has so far declined to endorse Netanyahu and has sidestepped questions on whether he should be reelected. “I’m not involved in [Israeli] politics anymore,” he told Time earlier this month. On Thursday, Trump told Newsmax Netanyahu would like him to be involved in the election. “I’ve had a very good relationship with him,” he said, but avoided endorsing him again. When asked directly whether he trusts Netanyahu, he said bluntly, “I don’t trust anybody in the world of politics.” For a campaign that has traditionally treated Netanyahu’s intimacy with the White House as a major electoral asset, the restraint is notable. Trump has starred in Netanyahu’s campaigns since 2013, when still a businessman and TV personality, he released a video urging Israelis to “vote for Benjamin.” When Trump entered the White House in 2017, he showered Netanyahu with political gifts. About two weeks before Israel’s April 2019 election, Netanyahu was in Washington to watch Trump sign a historic proclamation recognizing Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Golan Heights. In January 2020, five weeks before Israelis went again to the polls, Trump unveiled the Israeli-Palestinian “Deal of the Century” plan. Netanyahu stood smiling by his side. Ahead of this election, there has been no red carpet. The last time Netanyahu and Trump met at the White House in August, there were no cameras. The two did not meet at all when Netanyahu traveled to New York for the UN General Assembly in September. Over the course of the last year, Netanyahu has taken steps that have drawn fury from Trump, including undermining Trump-led peace efforts by striking inside Lebanon and Gaza. Trump has cursed the prime minister out in phone calls and warned him he’s losing support among Americans, according to people familiar with the conversations. He’s asked why Israel was blowing up apartment buildings in Lebanon and warned about the risk of a global economic downturn as a result of the Iran war. Inside the White House, many of the moves were interpreted as election-year posturing by Netanyahu, whose internal politics are well known by Trump and his advisers. Over the summer, many Trump advisers came to the conclusion that Netanyahu was trying to prolong the Iran war to bolster his own political standing. Trump has given Netanyahu a degree of leeway because of those political concerns, people familiar with the matter said. But he’s still grown frustrated at some of Israel’s actions, many of which he believes run counter to American interests. Another person close to Trump suggested his lack of endorsement is tied to Netanyahu’s weakness in the polls. Trump has long been careful to avoid endorsing candidates who seem likely to lose. In conversations over the past several months, Trump has quizzed Netanyahu about the election and his prospects, according to people familiar with the matter. While Netanyahu has sought to project confidence, Trump is well aware of the prime minister’s difficult political position. As Netanyahu’s standing fell in the Trump administration, so did Trump’s standing in Israel. According to Israeli sources close to Netanyahu, Trump was originally meant to be a centerpiece of Netanyahu’s campaign. Last December, at Mar-a-Lago, the prime minister announced that Trump would become the first non-Israeli to receive the prestigious Israel Prize. Netanyahu aides hoped Trump would accept the prize in person at Israel’s Independence Day ceremony in April, giving jumpstarting the campaign. Then came the war with Iran. The joint US-Israeli attack began on February 28 with the two leaders projecting strategic harmony. Netanyahu thanked “my friend, President Donald Trump,” calling him “a leader who stands by his word.” Trump described the two of them as “war heroes” and publicly demanded that Israel’s president grant Netanyahu a pardon in his ongoing corruption trials. But Trump never showed interest in attending the Israel Prize ceremony. By then, the fighting in Iran had ended and ceasefire talks were underway. The Iran ceasefire and subsequent memorandum of understanding were deeply unpopular in Israel, particularly on the right. Yinon Magal, a pro-Netanyahu TV anchor, called Trump a “loser” after the deal was signed. A July survey by the Jewish People Policy Institute found that only 7% of Israelis had “a great deal of trust” that Trump “will do the right thing” on US-Israel relations, and 45% had none. “Trump’s stock in Israel, especially among right wing-voters, has weakened,” a Likud source said. “An endorsement would not necessarily have helped Netanyahu so much, so he did not invest much in it.” Another Likud source said, “It’s not as if Trump will endorse any other opponent, so it’s nice to have, but not a must.” Netanyahu’s opponents are watching, but with less alarm than before. “A year ago, our camp was calling anyone close to Trump to prevent an endorsement,” one senior opposition figure said. “Now it doesn’t really matter, the charm is not there.” Another opposition source said they had conveyed messages urging the White House to stay out of the race and appreciated that Trump has so far done so. When Trump was asked specifically about who is currently polling as Netanyahu’s leading challenger, he said, “Well, I don’t know, I don’t hear bad things about him.” He then said, “They’ve written Bibi off many, many times, just like they’ve written me off many, many times. I wouldn’t underestimate Bibi.” Trump has his own reasons for distance. American public opinion of Israel has fallen sharply, declining even more against the backdrop of the Iran war. Israel’s average net favorability fell from +51 points in July 2018 to -16 in July 2026, according to multiple polls, a 67-point drop over eight years. As America quickly soured on the Iran war, a source familiar with the relationship said, Trump has been “trying to shed the image that Netanyahu pulled him into it.” Still, the apparent distance may be misleading. Israeli sources say the two leaders have recently discussed renewed strikes on Iran. Israeli security sources told CNN preparations are underway - pending Trump’s decision - with timing unclear because of the US midterm elections. Netanyahu rejected suggestions he was seeking escalation before the vote. “It is not convenient for us, it’s no good,” he told Army Radio this week. He complained that if Iran fired missiles at Israel, his opponents “will blame me.”

articles.title: Teen suspected of killing boy and stepmom was in prosecutors' sights for years — until new law let them strike
articles.summary: A legal gap in Indiana's juvenile jurisdiction law delayed murder charges for nearly two decades in the stabbing deaths of Blake and Chynna Dickus.
articles.body: Indiana investigators identified a suspect years before charging a man with the 2006 murders of 10-year-old Blake Dickus and his 26-year-old stepmother, Chynna Dickus, but prosecutors say an unusual gap in state law prevented them from bringing the case. Johnson County Prosecutor Lance Hamner told Fox News Digital that authorities had identified Michael Jerome James as a suspect in the double murders, but spent years working to establish a legal path to prosecute him for crimes he allegedly committed at age 14. "That's what took us so long," Hamner said. "We had a suspect identified. We weren't able to bring charges for several years because we were trying to get the jurisdictional statute in place." KILLER UNDONE BY DECADES-OLD THREADS — GLOVE, TOWEL AND SHIRT STITCH TOGETHER COLD CASE JUSTICE James, now 35, appeared in Johnson Circuit Court in Franklin on Thursday, Oct. 8, following a grand jury indictment in the July 24, 2006, deaths of Blake and Chynna. James faces four counts of murder. Prosecutors accuse him of killing Blake and Chynna while burglarizing or attempting to burglarize their Franklin home. During his court appearance, James told Johnson Circuit Court Judge Andrew Roesener that he did not have an attorney yet but planned to get one. Roesener gave James until Nov. 2 to hire an attorney and set his next status hearing for the same day. The legal gap that delayed prosecution for years James' age at the time of the killings is what created an unusual problem for the state, Hamner said. Indiana law historically gave juvenile courts jurisdiction over crimes committed by minors, creating a dilemma when authorities identified an alleged juvenile offender only after that person had aged out of the system. Since authorities did not identify or charge James while he was a juvenile, prosecutors faced the question of whether an adult court could legally hear the case. TEEN ACCUSED OF KILLING TWO GIRLS IN ALLEGED HIT-AND-RUN WILL BE TRIED AS ADULT AFTER IDENTITY REVEALED "That leaves a gap because this person is alleged to have committed a crime when he was 14, was not charged in juvenile court, and now that he's over the age of 18 could not be charged in adult court because of the way that law was written," Hamner said. In 2023, state law changed. A new legal path was created for adult courts to handle certain cases involving those accused of committing serious crimes as juveniles. The law did not cover every violent crime and depended partly on whether prosecutors could have sought adult prosecution when the offender was a juvenile. Hamner said another case involving child molestation allegations tested the 2023 statute. The Indiana Court of Appeals rejected its application in that case, and the Indiana Supreme Court later reached the same conclusion. "That means that we couldn't use it either," Hamner said. NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS "We started back over. We went back to the legislature and, with the guidance of the decision in that 2023 statute, drafted a new law that would satisfy the concerns that the Indiana Supreme Court had." Hamner said lawmakers passed a new statute in 2025 after considering the concerns raised by the Indiana Supreme Court. The 2025 change gave prosecutors the legal mechanism needed to charge James. "Then we were back in business to be able to charge this individual," he said. Hamner said he is more confident the latest statute will withstand a legal challenge. "Nothing's ever certain, but I'm a lot more confident about this statute than we were with the other one," Hamner said. Criminal defense lawyer Mike Cunningham, however, told Fox 59 News that he believes Indiana law does not allow prosecutors to charge James as an adult for crimes he allegedly committed before the state changed its juvenile jurisdiction law in 2023. "For acts that are committed after 2023, if you’re a juvenile and we don’t learn about it until after you’re 21, then you may be held accountable in adult court," he said. "But what the court has said is for anything that happened before 2023, the law does not permit that because they did not have adequate notice." If James' eventual defense attorney challenges the court's jurisdiction, the dispute could determine whether prosecutors can pursue the murder case at all. The investigation Blake and Chynna suffered multiple stab wounds inside the family's home on Aberdeen Drive in the otherwise peaceful Branigin Woods subdivision. Investigators determined that Blake also had blunt-force injuries and signs of smothering. Blake's father, Sean Dickus, returned home and discovered the bodies.
